case.pattern_description: Amount structuring: 4 online purchases between $456.96 and $488.04 within 30 minutes, each just under a $500 threshold, from 2 device profiles marked New. The amounts sit just below a $500 authorization threshold, which none of the five documented patterns describes; the same shape recurs on unrelated cardholders in the bank's closed cases. Found by scanning the card's one-hour window for repeated near-threshold online amounts.

evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3476682 ($482.12, product C, online) scores 0.18 on the calibrated transaction model trained only on the bank's closed cases (out-of-time AUC 0.964 vs 0.866 for the bank's risk score). The bank's own risk score was 0.25.
Card baseline from 199 earlier transactions: median $62.93, 95th percentile $414.69; the flagged amount is 7.7x the median.
Device profile 'Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080' was used by this card before; identity record marks it New.
The strongest transaction in the burst scores 0.67 on the same model (3476633); the episode is assessed at that level, not at the flagged transaction's.

Structuring: 4 online purchases between $456.96 and $488.04 within 30 minutes, each just under a $500 threshold, from 2 device profiles marked New. The bank's closed cases record the same shape five times (CC-3748, CC-3841, CC-3907, CC-4086, CC-4124), all confirmed fraud and filed as undocumented. Measured on July-October, such bursts are fraud 9 times in 45; on top of the model score, which already sees much of that, the shape is worth x1.64.

Cardholder C07297 reported the $482.12 charge as not theirs (case pack trigger, 2016-11-22 02:30:00). Measured on October: all 1,203 disputes the bank investigated were fraud, 15% of them scored under 0.05, so a low score does not clear a denial (1.00). If this is a planted dispute on a legitimate transaction, a score this size is 88.32x as likely on disputed fraud as on a legitimate transaction (0.99). Weighted equally: 0.99.
The known patterns are not the only ones: activity that fits none of them is described in the analyst's own words.
Policy R2: Customer denies the transaction: BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE; FILE_REPORT if exposure exceeds $1,000 or the case connects to a shared device profile or another card's fraud.

Policy §3a: A case is opened at probability 0.30, on any evidence request, or on any dispute; a report is filed only when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected and exposure exceeds $1,000, the activity connects to a shared device, region or another customer's fraud, or the pattern is coordinated or undocumented.
Policy R9: Undocumented coordinated abuse: CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT, ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST, and describe the pattern in your own words.

sar.narrative: Between 2016-11-21 and 2016-11-21, card C07297-K1 held by customer C07297 was used for 4 transaction(s) totalling $1,906.07 that the bank has determined were not authorised by the cardholder (transaction IDs 3476602, 3476633, 3476665, 3476682). The activity was online, from device profile(s) Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080; iOS Device | iOS 11.2.1 | mobile safari 11.0 | 2208x1242, billed to region code(s) 264, 476. The alert was raised on 2016-11-22 02:30:00 by customer report on transaction 3476682 ($482.12). The purchases were placed minutes apart with each amount just below $500, consistent with deliberately keeping each authorization under a review threshold; the bank has seen the identical shape on five other cardholders, all confirmed fraud. The cardholder disputed the activity. The card has been blocked pending reissue; this report is filed because fraud is suspected and exposure $1,906.07 exceeds $1,000; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (R9).
